pages.text:
This is Pabi.
This is her dog Boo.
Boo has a very clever nose.
They are going to find a rainbow
with Boo’s nose.
Let’s go!
pages.change: Pabi and her dog Boo set out to find a rainbow by smell
pages.question_created: How can a nose find a rainbow?
pages.page_turn_note: The quest is announced and the spread ends on a call to go.

notes: Pabi runs with her spotted dog Boo, who wears a rainbow-striped collar; a painted rainbow fills the right page
illustration.only_in_image: Boo's collar is striped in rainbow colours: a rainbow is with them from the first page, which the text never says.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Boo smells something green.
Sniff, sniff, sniff.
Boo finds smelly green socks.
Can we eat smelly green socks?
No!
Boo’s nose smells some green …
pages.change: The first green find is smelly socks, which cannot be eaten
pages.question_created: What green thing will the nose find next?
pages.page_turn_note: The spread ends on an unfinished line (the nose smells some green ...) completed by the food word after the turn.

notes: Boo holds a green sock in his mouth; Pabi pulls a disgusted face with her tongue out; a giant pair of stinking socks on the right
illustration.only_in_image: Pabi pulls a disgusted face with her tongue out while Boo carries a sock in his mouth.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Spinach!
Can we eat spinach?
Yes!
And green beans!
Crunchy beans and
salty spinach.
Can you think of something
green that is good to eat?
pages.change: The right green find: spinach and beans, which can be eaten
pages.question_created: Can the listener name a green food?
pages.page_turn_note: A question to the listener closes the spread; the turn carries the colour pattern on, not an answer.

notes: Pabi smiles beside a vegetable bed with spinach and a bean plant; Boo sniffs the ground; beans and spinach shown large on the right
illustration.only_in_image: The food grows in a garden bed: spinach plants and a bean stalk in soil, a setting the text never names.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Boo smells something red.
Sniff, sniff, sniff.
Oh! Boo smells red soap.
Can we eat this red soapy soap?
No!
Boo’s nose smells some red …
pages.change: The red find is soap, which cannot be eaten
pages.question_created: What red thing will the nose find next?
pages.page_turn_note: Unfinished line (some red ...) completed after the turn.

notes: Boo has his head stuck inside an orange bucket over a bar of soap on a cloth; Pabi watches in surprise
illustration.only_in_image: Boo has pushed his whole head into an upturned bucket to reach the soap; Pabi watches open-mouthed.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Tomatoes!
Can we eat tomatoes?
Yes!
And beetroot!
Tasty tomatoes and
beautiful beetroot!
Can you think of something
red that is good to eat?
pages.change: The right red find: tomatoes and beetroot
pages.question_created: Can the listener name a red food?
pages.page_turn_note: Question to the listener; the turn continues the colour pattern.

notes: Pabi, hands on hips, and Boo look up at a tomato vine; a tomato and a beetroot shown large on the right

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Boo smells something orange.
Sniff, sniff, sniff.
Boo smells an orange bottle.
Can we eat a bottle?
No!
Boo’s nose smells an orange …
pages.change: The orange find is a bottle, which cannot be eaten
pages.question_created: What orange thing will the nose find next?
pages.page_turn_note: Unfinished line (an orange ...) completed by the fruit after the turn: the word is both colour and food.

notes: a baby sits on a play mat among building blocks with an orange-handled sippy bottle; Pabi stands beside him, Boo sits nearby
illustration.only_in_image: The bottle belongs to a baby sitting among building blocks; the baby is never mentioned in the text.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Pumpkin!
Can we eat pumpkin?
Yes!
And oranges!
Sweet, juicy oranges and
spicy pumpkin.
Can you think of something
orange that is good to eat?
pages.change: The right orange find: pumpkin and oranges
pages.question_created: Can the listener name an orange food?
pages.page_turn_note: Question to the listener; the turn continues the colour pattern.

notes: Pabi laughs with a small pumpkin balanced on her head, Boo leaping beside her; an orange and a pumpkin on the right
illustration.only_in_image: Pabi laughs with the pumpkin balanced on her head while Boo leaps beside her.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Boo smells something yellow.
Sniff, sniff, sniff.
Boo smells her yellow ball.
Can we eat Boo’s yellow ball?
No!
Boo’s nose smells some yellow …
pages.change: The yellow find is a ball, which cannot be eaten
pages.question_created: What yellow thing will the nose find next?
pages.page_turn_note: Unfinished line (some yellow ...) completed after the turn.

notes: Pabi frowns with hands on hips; Boo crouches playfully near a tennis ball; a large worn tennis ball on the right
illustration.only_in_image: Pabi stands with hands on hips and a frown while Boo crouches to play: her impatience with the fourth wrong find is only in the picture.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Mielies!
Can we eat mielies?
Yes!
And bananas!
Crunchy, crispy mielies and
beautiful, big bananas.
Can you think of something
yellow that is good to eat?
pages.change: The right yellow find: mielies and bananas
pages.question_created: Can the listener name a yellow food?
pages.page_turn_note: Question to the listener; the colour pattern ends here.

notes: Pabi laughs and points at Boo, who balances a banana on his head; she carries mielies in a cloth bag; a mielie cob and bananas on the right
illustration.only_in_image: Boo balances a banana on his head and Pabi carries mielies in a cloth on her back.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Boo and Pabi found green beans.
And red tomatoes.
And orange pumpkin.
And yellow mielies.
How beautiful!
‘Can we make a
rainbow, Boo?’
asks Pabi.
pages.action: lists the finds and has an idea
pages.change: The four colour finds are gathered and Pabi asks whether they can make a rainbow from them
pages.page_turn_note: A direct question at the spread end is answered after the turn (Yes! Look!).

notes: the four found foods grouped on the left; Pabi bends down face to face with Boo on the right

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Yes!
Look!
‘We are cooking a big, juicy,
sweet, crispy, beautiful
rainbow,’ says Pabi.
‘Can we eat our
rainbow, Boo?’
pages.change: The finds are being cooked into a rainbow meal
pages.page_turn_note: The title question is asked of Boo at the spread end and answered after the turn.

notes: an adult in a leaf-patterned apron, seen only from the shoulders down, stands at a kitchen counter; Pabi on a step stool watches; Boo sits by his bowl
illustration.only_in_image: An adult in an apron, shown only from the shoulders down, does the cooking at the counter while Pabi watches from a step stool; the text says only that they are cooking.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
‘Yes, we can!
Our rainbow tastes good!
It makes us big and strong!’
You can eat a
rainbow too!
pages.change: They eat the rainbow, and the narrator tells the listener they can too
pages.page_turn_note: last page; a wordless vignette follows

notes: Pabi eats beetroot from a fork at a spotted table with plates of the cooked colourful foods and a chicken drumstick; Boo peeks over the table edge; a rainbow behind them
illustration.only_in_image: The meal also holds a chicken drumstick and sliced fruit not found on the hunt, and a painted rainbow with blue and purple bands rises behind the table although only four colours were found.
